benchmark report · 2026-06-11

Local vs hosted Vaadin docs MCP — a Claude-only A/B/C

Today's sweep drops Codex and pits three Claude Opus 4.8 variants against the same three Vaadin tasks: skills + hosted docs MCP, skills + local docs MCP, and the no-skills baseline. Same two-phase solve→verify pipeline. The question: does the local MCP change the answer?

the one fail is a known harness hang, not a solver miss
  • The local Vaadin docs MCP is a drop-in for the hosted one. claude-local-mcp and claude (hosted) score identically on every rubric — 21 vs 20 on basic_layout (local edges it), 31 = 31 on basic_form, 47 = 47 on md_ui_spec. No quality regression from running docs locally.
  • basic_form: all three scored a perfect 31/31 — including the no-skills baseline, which fixed yesterday's Aura radio/checkbox orientation miss. A vivid reminder that single-run deltas are noisy.
  • Skills still earn their keep on the hard problem. On md_ui_spec both skill variants beat the baseline 47 vs 45 — the baseline lost a drawer focus-ring clip and mixed Aura + Lumo theme variants.
  • The 480px breakpoint bug is back — again, on all three. Same root cause as yesterday (max-width: 379.98px never triggers at the rubric's 480px narrow test). A new inline-style ding (getStyle().set("min-height","0")) also hit all three on basic_layout.
  • One row was killed mid-record. claude-local-mcp's basic_layout solve exited 143 (SIGTERM) — the documented agent-SDK hang where the solver finishes its work but never exits and the timeout reaps it. Phase 2 graded that very workspace 21/24 (best of three), so the app was built fine; only the phase-1 row (cost + trace) is missing.

Identical to yesterday's finding — strong evidence the task's "narrow" definition (or the skeleton) nudges this breakpoint.

Same 480px miss (−2) and inline style (−1), plus Content area (−1): toolbars and content share one transparent surface — no border/shadow/contrast, so no visual separator distinguishes them.

Worst narrow-viewport result (1/4): groups on one row at 480, items don't grow, and the Text Field measures only 92px at 375 (under the 100px floor). Plus the same inline style (−1).

no-skills−3

Lost the Composite<FormLayout> point too, plus Layout (−1: in the drawer the FormLayout sits flush in an overflow:auto Scroller, so edge fields' focus rings get clipped) and Vaadin-specific (−1: mixes Aura + Lumo — the ConfirmDialog uses setConfirmButtonTheme("error primary"), a Lumo variant, in an Aura-themed app).

Skills delta: +2 (47 vs 45). Both skill variants avoided the theme-mixing and focus-clip traps the baseline fell into.

7 Cross-cutting observations

Local MCP is a clean substitute

The core question this run answers: serving the Vaadin docs from a local MCP yields the same rubric outcomes and the same cost as the hosted one (21/31/47 vs 20/31/47). No measured downside — useful if you want to run the bench offline or pin a docs version.

The 480px bug reproduces

Two days, two independent sweeps, same max-width: 379.98px chosen by every agent and the same lost narrow-viewport bullets at 480px. This is now firmly a benchmark-level signal — worth clarifying the task's narrow-viewport definition before reading the basic_layout spread as an agent skill gap.

Single-run deltas are noisy

The no-skills baseline went from losing basic_form's orientation point yesterday to a perfect 31/31 today, and basic_layout drifted 1–3 points across the board. Treat any ±1–2 swing as variance; the durable signals are the recurring bug and the md_ui_spec skills gap.

Skills matter most where the spec is hardest

Skills made no rubric difference on basic_form (all maxed) and a small one on basic_layout, but a clear +2 on md_ui_spec — the densest spec, where idiom (Composite, theme consistency) and edge-case polish (focus rings) decide the last few points.

8 Caveats & data gaps

  • The killed row. claude-local-mcp / basic_layout exited 143 (SIGTERM) — the agent-SDK finished its work but didn't exit, so the per-row timeout reaped it. Its phase-1 cost/trace are lost ($0, blank), but the workspace was complete and phase 2 graded it 21/24. Don't read the 66.7% pass-rate on eval-Q5b as a solver failure.
  • Self-grading is total this run (no Codex) — every grade is Claude-on-Claude. Fine for the local-vs-hosted question (same grader both sides); take the absolute scores as Claude's own measurement.
  • Token columns understate throughput by design; the cache-rd figures are the real numbers from metadata.modelUsage. Use cost, not tokens, for efficiency.
  • n = 1 per cell, and today's basic_form sweep (all 31/31) shows how much a single run can move. Re-run with REPEAT=N for anything you want to treat as a ranking.
